name: Cressbrook Homestead
scope: Cressbrook main homestead assembly: the principal House and secondary Cottage with their intrinsic attached domestic wings/verandas/roof structures. Retain two distinct dwellings and an open space between them; do not collapse the estate into one generic house or extrude its parcel. House has gabled/attic roof forms and attached low veranda wings; explicit Cottage source shows low hipped roof/wrap veranda and chimneys. Include timber/slab/weatherboard walls, own veranda posts/rails, doors/windows, roof junctions/chimneys and short domestic steps. Exclude separate chapel, stables/dairy/worker cabins/explosives store/water-tank frames, whole farm grounds/tennis court/river/trees/fences/people and interior.
era: Surviving nineteenth-century main homestead dwellings based on exact published1899/circa1930/undated public-domain originals. Primary heritage description confirms both principal homes and north-facing House/rear domestic courtyard. Current colors, later changes, dimensions/hidden wings and exact geographic component positions remain estimates.

references.filename: StateLibQld 1 95648 Cressbrook dwelling, The Cottage, overlooking the Brisbane River near Toogoolawah.jpg
references.caption:
Cressbrook dwelling, The Cottage, overlooking the Brisbane River near Toogoolawah
Cressbrook was established in 1841 by David McConnel and his brother John in the Brisbane Valley. It was the first pastoral run to be settled east of the Great Dividing Range in the Moreton Bay District. They farmed the land and ran beef cattle. Later they established a condensed milk factory in the area.The original homestead at Cressbrook is still standing, and is still owned by the McConnel family, the fourth generation of ownership.

review.method: Four exact published Qualla/SLQoriginals/native explicit archive grants/item handles/SHA1 inspected, including named Cottage identity.
review.notes: Qualla-first full15-source-family inventory with no conflicts. Four exact published SLQpublic-domain originals actually inspected:1899homestead rear/gables,1930wide gable/attic homestead, circa1930front low hipped/veranda view and explicit Cottage overlooking river. Native SHA1s, exact archive item handles and explicit PD-Australia/StateLibQld-License match. Photographer fields are unrecorded in both Qualla and native archive records; exact hash-bound item releases qualify without inventing attribution, and no named credit is overridden. Explicit Cottage caption prevents confusing its low hipped/veranda form with the principal gabled/attic House. Other family portraits, distant trees/horse paddocks and attribution media unused. No external photography/copied pixels/generated bitmap. Primary Queensland Heritage Register text only for identity/arrangement; its modern photos/maps unused.
